title: Rule one: never fold what you didn't wash 🧺
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: Rule one: never fold what you did not wash.

scenes.narration: Rule one: never fold what you did not wash.
You have been hired as the night attendant at Wash House Twenty-Four. One room. Ten machines. No customers after four.
Rule two: if a customer stays past four, offer them a chair. Do not offer them conversation.
Rule three: the dryer on the left runs without coins. Let it finish. Never open it early.
Rule four: if the lights begin to hum a tune, do not hum along.
Rule five: lost property goes in the blue crate. If something in the crate moves, close the lid.
Rule six: the last customer will always thank you before leaving. Say, you are welcome. Nothing else.
Tonight, the left dryer is running. The lights hum a tune you almost recognise. The crate lid is quivering.
Then you find a seventh rule, written at the bottom, in fresh ink. Rule seven: nobody has ever thanked you.
Behind you, a voice, soft and close, over your shoulder. Thank you. You were so kind to fold me.
So tell me. Do you turn around, or keep folding?
